scope: Read-only local source/configuration audit of distinct A/B pairs, one exclusive L40 per process. Not a cross-node filesystem test, throughput benchmark, or evidence of multi-GPU numerical/research benefit.
conclusion: Frozen implementation is structured for cross-pair concurrency without DDP, batch/schedule changes, or concurrent writers to one pair. No concrete source-level race requiring modification of the173-file snapshot was found.

findings.detail: Exactly one visible GPU is required. Per-stage nonblocking flock and per-output training lock prevent simultaneous pair writes. A then B remains sequential within each pair. The registered36 run/checkpoint roots are distinct.

Each key uses one of256 flock stripes. Reads hold BEGIN IMMEDIATE through file SHA verification and torch.load, excluding eviction. Missing-feature GPU build is outside the SQLite transaction while the stripe remains held. Shared black is obtained before entering the window stripe; no DB-to-stripe lock inversion was found.

UUID temporary tensor writes, fsync and atomic replace occur under the DB transaction. Eviction removes index entries before file deletion; deletion rechecks absence under a new transaction, protecting concurrent republication. Orphan cleanup is transaction-locked. Payload identity/SHA corruption fails closed.

Feature identity binds suite/base/data/statistics/source and intentionally omits seed/budget. Feature generation uses frozen detached computations and restores RNG. Pair-local seeded initialization/order, batch8 and5000-update schedule remain unchanged. This does not prove bitwise equality across hardware or drivers.

The shared128GiB per-suite bound does not grow with worker count. SQLite serializes reads/publications; stripe collisions and cache churn can idle allocated GPUs or cause the600s SQLite timeout. Additional recomputation may affect the ongoing first pair cost. Do not assume linear throughput or unchanged cost.

HF module/hub cache is shared within a suite. Existing Long cache is warmed by completed runs. Keep dependencies, module caches and immutable weights unchanged during concurrent execution; new suites first pass their single registered acceptance before launching their own pairs. No external-library concurrent cold-cache implementation was tested here.

Root submission/state changes stay serialized under the supervisor lock; different stage keys may run concurrently. An unresolved sbatch leaves pending_submission and prevents subsequent submissions. Preserve scheduler CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and request one GPU per independent pair; never submit a second job to the current pair.

runtime_limits.recommendation: For same-suite multi-node sharing, root should establish the actual filesystem lock/atomic-rename behavior with a small dedicated CPU-only lock probe if not already evidenced. Independent-suite acceptance jobs use separate caches and can overlap immediately within existing resource limits. This is not a request to change the frozen cache or scientific configuration.

minimal_execution_plan: Keep3012151 running; never touch its current invocation, checkpoint or cache configuration.

Root registers/submits distinct stage keys serially, but lets jobs execute concurrently. Use one exclusive L40,7CPUs,64GiB memory per existing wrapper; leave batch8,5000updates,selection and500-step engineering boundaries unchanged.
Overlap remaining suite-specific acceptance stages. Only after each suite real F00/F01/F03 and root review pass may its registered pairs start.

For accepted suites, schedule distinct budget/seed pairs in parallel with unique registered run/checkpoint roots; keep A/B internal order and explicit resume rules. Start with a small concurrent set and use observed lock-wait/cache churn/GPU utilization to determine an operational cap, without searching scientific parameters.

Preserve all per-job cache journals/failures and one Slurm allocation charge per job. Nested cache timers are diagnostic, not an additional GPU bill; do not claim independent-training cost or speedup from concurrency alone.
